vision_features.image_context: Close-up overhead view of a soybean plant at or near harvest maturity, lying on or very close to the ground. Multiple stems and numerous seed pods are visible. The background shows dry soil, crop debris, and dried plant material.
vision_features.abnormalities: 1. Stems: The main stems running through the center and upper portion of the image display irregular mottled patterning consisting of dark gray-to-black blotches and streaks on an otherwise tan-to-olive-green background. These dark markings are irregular in shape, ranging from small (2–5 mm) spots to elongated streaks (10–30 mm), distributed along the length of the visible stems. The surface texture of the affected stem areas appears slightly roughened or pitted compared to the surrounding stem tissue. 2. Pods: The majority of pods are uniformly dry and golden-tan to light brown, consistent with mature/dry-down stage. However, many pods show a mottled or speckled surface texture with small, slightly darker tan-brown flecks scattered across the pod surface. Some pods also appear slightly shriveled or flattened, suggesting possible underfilling. The pods are covered in fine, short, pale golden hairs (trichomes) giving a fuzzy texture. 3. On certain pods, faint whitish-gray patches of a dry, slightly powdery or chalky deposit are visible, primarily at the base and along the seams of the pods, in patches of approximately 3–8 mm across.
vision_features.absences: 1. No green tissue is visible anywhere on the plant — all tissue is fully dry and tan/brown, consistent with late-season senescence. 2. No visible liquid exudate or wet, slimy areas on any organ. 3. No raised pustules, blister-like structures, or orange/rust-colored powdery deposits on pods or stems. 4. No obvious insect bodies, feeding damage holes, or gall-like swellings are visible on the pods or stems.
vision_features.summary: The image shows a fully mature, dry soybean plant with numerous golden-tan seed pods lying on bare soil amid crop debris. The most striking feature is the dark gray-to-black mottled blotching along the main stems, which contrasts sharply with the otherwise uniform tan coloration of the dry plant material. The pods themselves appear mostly mature and hairy but show some mild surface speckling and flattening suggestive of incomplete seed fill. The stems are the most visually abnormal organ, with the dark irregular patterning being the single most unusual visual feature in the image.
